title: Return Decomposition of Hybrid Strategies in the Brazilian Market: Evidence of Genuine Alpha and Factor Exposure
abstract: arXiv:2611.06919v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper decomposes the return sources of a hybrid portfolio combining a fundamentalist screen - based on P/E, ROE, Net Margin, Current Ratio, and P/BV - with a moving-average crossover system (SMA 9/46), applied to the Brazilian stock exchange (B3) from January 2000 to December 2025 (300 monthly observations). CAPM and Fama-French three- and four-factor models estimated by OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors identify a positive and statistically significant Jensen alpha of 1.11% per month (p = 0.005) in the three-factor model. In the four-factor model with momentum, alpha remains significant (0.98% p.m.; p = 0.009), while momentum is not significant (p = 0.409). The central - and unexpected - finding is the non-significance of the HML factor (beta_h = 0.1266; p = 0.544): despite explicit value criteria, returns do not load on the value premium, likely because ROE and Net Margin tilt selection toward quality firms. translated_title: 巴西市场混合策略的收益分解：真实Alpha与因子暴露的证据
translated_abstract: 本文分解了一个混合投资组合的收益来源，该组合将基于市盈率（P/E）、净资产收益率（ROE）、净利率、流动比率和市净率（P/BV）的基本面筛选与移动平均线交叉系统（SMA 9/46）相结合，应用于巴西证券交易所（B3），样本期为2000年1月至2025年12月（300个月度观测值）。通过采用异方差稳健标准误的普通最小二乘法（OLS）估计的CAPM以及Fama-French三因子和四因子模型，在三因子模型中识别出正向且统计显著的Jensen alpha，为每月1.11%（p = 0.005）。在包含动量因子的四因子模型中，alpha仍然显著（每月0.98%；p = 0.009），而动量因子不显著（p = 0.409）。核心——也是出乎意料的——发现是HML因子不显著（beta_h = 0.1266；p = 0.544）：尽管明确采用了价值筛选标准，收益却并未对价值溢价产生载荷，这可能是因为ROE和净利率使选股偏向高质量公司。
tldr: 本文分解了巴西市场中基本面筛选与均线交叉技术系统相结合的混合策略收益来源，发现策略在控制多因子风险后仍具有每月约1%的显著真实Alpha，但出乎意料的是价值因子（HML）并不显著，表明ROE和净利率等质量指标使选股偏向高质量公司，从而掩盖了价值溢价。
en_tdlr: This paper decomposes the returns of a hybrid strategy combining fundamental screening with a moving-average crossover system on the Brazilian market, finding significant genuine alpha of roughly 1% per month after factor controls, yet an unexpected non-significance of the value (HML) factor, suggesting that quality-oriented criteria (ROE and net margin) drive selection away from value premium exposure.
